newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

-- A record 3,263 business entities out of a total of 10,389 inspected in July 1997 by the finance ministry's recently established team of 'untouchables' will be fined an aggregate 4.6 billion drachmas for around 57,000 breaches of tax and customes regulations.

-- The deputy finance minister George Drys has set August 25 as the deadline for completion of processing of some 1,000,000 income tax statements by regional fiscal revenue services which have yet to be forwarded to the ministry for electronic cross-checking.

-- A new bill drafted by the labour ministry is expected to remove regidities in hirings to Greece's civil service whereby priority was offerd on social grounds to population groups including the handicapped, descendants of national resistance members, and members of large families.

-- The government is concerned with the lukewarm welcome of Monday's issue of inflation-protected treasury paper by the investment public in view of its large fiscal needs in September -- 2.0 billion drachmas. Currently, returns on treasury paper are less appealing than bank deposit rates.

-- During its first four months of operations, the finance ministry's tax crime force (SDOE) has imposed fines totalling 14.6 billion drachmas on 150,707 breaches of tax regulations by a total of 5,644 businesses.

-- The industrial reconstruction organisation (OAE) has run into difficulties in its efforts to privatise Elefsis Bauxites SA because its former administration --the Skalistiris group-- had placed its assets as collaterals for debt raised by other group entities from National Bank of Greece.

-- The efficacy of the government's economic policy to be followed in 1998 will rely upon its ability to harness public spending. Government officials admit there is no scope for a rise in taxation and point out that the recent cut in the gasoline tax proves that the government sticks to its anti-inflationary policy.
-- The union of Greece's retailers favour a return to a shorter sales season and more effective administrative controls over aggressive discounts by some retailers who hinder competition.

-- The Public Investment Programme included in the 1998 Budget which is being drafted will amount to 1.2 trillion drachmas, up 20 percent on the previous year, in order to speed up infastructure works co-funded by the European Union.
-- The government will decide in September which public entities and civil services are to be dismantled or merged as part of its cost-cutting efforts.

-- The cost of transfer of ownership of vehicles for business use will be wiped out following a decision by the transportation ministry to comply with relevant European Union regulations. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
